preview: Interview experience at Deutsche Bank for an FTE role detailing online coding rounds, technical interviews, professional fitness, and HR rounds.
content: INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE DEUTSCHE BANK Prerna Jagesia, B.Tech Computers (2019 - 23) Round 1 - Online coding round (90 mins) The test was held on the HackerEarth platform. There were 110+ students who gave the coding round. The test consisted of 3 questions, one for 20 marks and the other two for 50 marks each. 1) Find whether the given number is Armstrong or not: (20 marks) https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/program-for-armstrong-numbers/ 2) Given two arrays A [a1,.......,an] and B[b1,.....,bn], you need to make the first array equal to the second(order of elements does not matter) in minimum number of moves such that (50 marks) for 0 <= i,j < n, A[i] = A[i] + 2 & A[j] =A[j] - 2 stands for one move Output the minimum number of moves if it is possible to convert A to B else output -1. Example 1) : Input: A = [2,5,6] , B = [1,2,10] Output: 2 Explanation: Move 1) In array A, we modify (2,3) indices [considering 1-based indexing] So A = [2, 5 -2, 6+2] = [2,3,8] Move 2) In array A, we modify (2,3) indices [considering 1-based indexing] So A = [2, 3 -2, 8+2] = [2,1,10] Example 2) : Input: A = [2,4,6] , B = [1,2,10] Output : -1 Explanation: Not possible to convert A to B because the difference between the elements is not even. Example 3): Input: A = [0,2,8] , B = [2,4,6] Output : -1 3) Consider that you have been given the current state of a parking lot such that numbers > 1 stand for a car, -1 stands for a pillar, and 0 stands for an empty parking space. Find the minimum number of moves required to transform the current state of the parking lot into a given desired state such that each move can be either forward or backward in an empty space. ( 50 marks) Example 1): Input: Current_array = [-1,1,0,2] , Desired_array = [-1,1,2,0] Output: 1 Input: Current_array = [-1,8,0,6,7,4,0,2] , Desired_array = [-1,8,6,7,2,4,0,0] Output: -1 29 people were shortlisted for the interviews. Round 2 - Technical Interview round (~60 mins) 1. Tell me about yourself 2. What was your favourite subject in college? I replied DSA. So he asked me more of DSA problems than other CS fundamentals. 3. Find the lowest common ancestor given two nodes in a BST. 4. What is a threaded binary tree? I was not able to answer this :/ 5. Sort an array consisting of only 0s and 1s - I gave the brute force solution first and then optimized it using two pointers https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/segregate-0s-and-1s-in-an-array-by-traversing-array-once/ 6. Given an array of arbitrary length, find the nth smallest element in the array (without sorting obviously :)) I gave him the approach of using quicksort. When the index returned by the partition method of quicksort is equal to n-1 (because of 0-based indexing), we should break from the function and return the element at that index. He was expecting the approach of using heapsort but looked satisfied with my answer. All the approaches can be found here: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/kth-smallestlargest-element-unsorted-array/ You can use a priority queue instead of building the heap from scratch. 7. Given two numbers, how to find the GCD/HCF of those numbers - https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/c-program-find-gcd-hcf-two-numbers/ 8. What are the disadvantages of recursion? 9. What is dynamic programming? Mention these two very important properties in your answer - optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems. He then moved on to simple DBMS questions like: 10. What is normalization in databases and explain the three normal forms? 11. What is indexing in databases? (Just the concept, not the implementation) 12. Given two table structures, what will be the best way to model a one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relationship. For one to many and many to one, we should add the primary key of the table with one record as the foreign key of the table with many records. For many-to-many relationship, create a separate table with a mapping of the primary keys of the related records. 13. What work did you do during your internship? 14. Explain ACID properties The interview concluded after this and 14 people made it to the third round Round 3 - Technical Interview round (~60 mins) 1. Tell me about yourself. 2. How to build a queue from a linked list? 3. Can there be more than one primary key in a table? NO. 4. Can there be more than one foreign key in a table? YES 5. Can there be more than one unique key in a table? YES 6. Given two tables - employee table (with employee ID, employee name, salary and Dept ID as attributes) and department table (with Dept ID and Dept. Name as attributes) a. Write a query to print the Dept. ID and sum of salaries in each department. b. Write a query to print the employee name and department name of each employee. 7. He then moved to my resume and asked a few basic questions about the projects I had mentioned like what is the role of package.json file in Node.js and what was the structure of my MongoDB database 8. Elaborate on the work done during your internship After these questions, he asked me if I had any questions for him. Always ask questions as it shows your interest in the company. I asked him how projects and teams will be allotted to new joiners. He explained the process and the interview concluded. 12 people were shortlisted for the next round. Round 4 - Professional Fitness Round (~30 mins) This round consisted of simple behavioral and situational questions. Here they evaluate whether you are a fit for their company. 1. Tell me about yourself. (It can get boring ik :/) 2. What is your family background? 3. Consider a scenario where you and your team are having a group discussion and you suggest a solution to some problem. But the senior people in your team dismiss your solution without proper reason. What will you do in this case? 4. Consider a case where you work on a project and deploy it to production. Now a bug arises in the code while in production which is causing some impact on the business of the company. You are called over the weekend to investigate the issue. You find that you can either provide a quick fix for the bug in two days or provide a proper fix for the bug in 3-4 weeks. What will you do in this situation? 5. What are some challenges I encountered in my previous internship experience? She then asked me if I had some questions for her. I asked her about her experience so far at Deutsche bank. Everyone who gave the ProFit round was asked to give the HR round as well. Round 5 - HR Round (~25-30 mins) 1. Tell me about yourself. 2. Since I had to go to the Bangalore office for my internship, I was asked about my experience there. What did I learn in my previous company and similar questions. 3. Explain how does a bank make money? They wanted just the basics of it -Banks generally make money by borrowing money from depositors and compensating them with a certain interest rate. The banks will lend the money out to borrowers, charging the borrowers a higher interest rate and profiting off the interest rate spread. 4. If you see people misusing the money of the company, for example, taking reimbursement for first class tickets while they actually travel in the second class, what will you do? 5. If you see someone be a victim of sexual harassment and is scared to speak up, what will you do? 6. If you see some team member who used to perform very well earlier suddenly underperform and not be able to concentrate on his/her work, what action will you take? 7. How do you keep yourself updated with what’s going on in the world? 8. Do you read? The interview concluded with him explaining to me the different qualities people should have to become a leader at a bank. All the 12 people who gave round 4 and 5 were selected :) Resources used: 1. Apna college YT channel 2. Leetcode 3. Interview bit 4. Gfg (not for questions, but just for solutions to questions I didn't understand) Tips: 1. Keep some hard copies of your resume handy. Since some companies take offline interviews, they do ask for hard copies. 2. Be very thorough with your CS fundamentals. Don’t neglect it and leave it for the end. 3. When you don’t understand a particular problem statement, do ask for clarifications on it. 4. Think out loud. This way the interviewer gets an idea about which direction you are headed and may help you start thinking in the right direction. This also keeps the interview interactive. 5. Make sure to go through all projects on your resume and be prepared for questions that can be asked about them like why did you use this technology/framework instead of that technology/framework, difference between two frameworks, etc. 6. It is alright to tell them that you don’t know a particular thing instead of bluffing about it and getting caught. They don’t expect you to know everything. They are more interested in seeing how you use the knowledge you have and apply your logic to tackle an unseen problem statement. Lastly, keep calm during your interviews and have confidence in yourself. All the best !!👍 If you have any queries, feel free to drop an email at pkjagesia@gmail.com
